title: Cyrus and the Salt
premise: Mara Lockridge has spent nine years as the king's food-taster, swallowing small poisons so the crown doesn't have to, and mapping smuggler roads through the Thornfell mountains as her private escape plan. When prayers to the old gods suddenly begin working again—crops rising overnight, the dying healed—the court's quiet rot surfaces: King Aldric is bound body and soul to a thing wearing his crown, an ancient hunger that feeds on devotion and has been drinking the kingdom's faith for a generation. As the moon counts toward its thirteenth turn, when the binding will become permanent, Mara must choose between the loyalty that kept her alive and the truth that could free them all. In the end she breaks the binding at the cost of her own hard-won immunity—taking into herself the last of the old god's hunger—and walks out of the palace alive but no longer invisible, carrying a king who remembers what he was.
about_author: Beatrix Coldharbour is the pen name of a former line cook who swears the best fantasy is written by people who know what it costs to feed other people. She lives near a mountain pass and writes about loyalty, salt, and the lies we swallow to survive.

chapters.title: The Taster's Tongue
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. She tastes the king's evening meal, detects bitter almond in the honeyed quail, and saves his life without ceremony. Establishes her numb competence, her scarred tongue, and her secret map of Thornfell smuggler roads hidden under a floorboard. Emotional beat: weary pride in a job no one thanks her for.

chapters.title: Thirteen Moons
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The court astrologer announces the coming thirteenth turn of the moon—an omen no one can name. Mara notices the king flinch when the old gods are mentioned, and that his shadow moves a half-second late. Emotional beat: first cold prickle of wrongness beneath routine.

chapters.title: Salt on the Tongue
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. A shipment of consecrated salt arrives from the mountain shrines; tasting it, Mara hears a whisper no one else does. She visits the palace kitchens and finds the head cook praying to a god whose name hasn't been spoken in decades—and getting an answer. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into fear.

chapters.title: The Thing Wearing His Crown
chapters.summary: King Aldric's POV, brief and fragmented. Inside the king's mind: a vast patient presence wearing his memories like borrowed clothes, savoring the taste of renewed prayer. He cannot remember his daughter's face. Emotional beat: drowning quietly in one's own skull.

chapters.title: Smuggler's Road
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Sent to meet a Thornfell informant about poisoned grain, Mara travels her old routes and finds shrine-keepers lighting fires again along the passes. Her informant begs her to carry a petition to the gods on the court's behalf. Emotional beat: the past reaching for her despite her invisibility.

chapters.title: The Devouring Kind
chapters.summary: Sera Vane, the king's spymaster, POV. Sera has been tracking the surge of answered prayers and the disappearances of priests who ask too many questions. She suspects the crown itself and begins watching Mara, the only taster whose reports never vary. Emotional beat: professional suspicion sharpening into dread.

chapters.title: What the Cook Knew
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The head cook is found dead, kneeling, smiling, hollowed out like a eaten fruit. Mara finds a note in the man's flour-dusted hand: 'It drinks the faithful. Do not pray where it can hear.' Emotional beat: grief weaponized into resolve.

chapters.title: The Tenth Turn
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV. The presence grows stronger with each answered prayer; Aldric claws back three minutes of control during a council meeting and scribbles a warning no one deciphers. Mara, serving wine, recognizes his handwriting from old ledgers. Emotional beat: a flicker of the man inside the mask.

chapters.title: Immunity
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Flashback chapter: how a starving border girl became the royal taster, dosed with poison until poison became her only constant companion. Reveals why belonging to the palace cost her everything soft. Emotional beat: understanding the price already paid.

chapters.title: Spymaster's Bargain
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Sera confronts Mara with evidence of her smuggler contacts and offers a choice: spy on the mountain shrines or hang for treason. Mara agrees—but plans to play both sides. Emotional beat: coerced alliance, mutual distrust.

chapters.title: Shrine of the First Salt
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. In the high passes, Mara meets the last true priestess, Ivenna, who explains the binding: generations ago the crown made a covenant with a famine-god, trading worship for survival, and the god has worn every king since. Emotional beat: awe and horror at the scale of the lie.

chapters.title: The God That Answers
chapters.summary: Ivenna's POV. The famine-god stirs in its mountain prison, drunk on new prayer, testing its strength by raising a dead shepherd. Ivenna realizes the thirteenth moon will complete the covenant permanently. Emotional beat: a guardian realizing she is too late.

chapters.title: Court of Whispers
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Back at court, Mara plays informant for Sera while feeding false trails. She watches the queen—hollow-eyed, complicit—pour out elaborate devotions that visibly strengthen the king. Emotional beat: revulsion at devotion as a feeding mechanism.

chapters.title: The Queen's Confession
chapters.summary: Queen Isolde's POV. Isolde knows what her husband carries; her family brokered the original covenant and her prayers keep him docile. She confesses to Mara not from kindness but because she needs a taster's help poisoning the god's next offering. Emotional beat: guilt dressed as duty.

chapters.title: Poisoning a God
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara and Isolde lace a ceremonial feast with consecrated salt and hellebore. For one night the king wakes—truly wakes—and begs Mara to find Ivenna before the twelfth turn. Emotional beat: desperate hope in a stolen hour of clarity.

chapters.title: Hunted Through Thornfell
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Sera discovers Mara's double game. Fleeing through her own smuggler roads with Sera's hunters behind her, Mara uses every hidden path she ever mapped. Emotional beat: the escape plan built over nine years finally used—for someone else's sake.

chapters.title: The Price of the Pass
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. To shake pursuit, Mara collapses a ravine crossing, killing two hunters—one of them a boy who once ran messages for her. Emotional beat: survival costing exactly what she feared it would.

chapters.title: Ivenna's Terms
chapters.summary: Ivenna's POV. Mara reaches the shrine; Ivenna reveals the unbinding requires a vessel willing to hold the god's hunger—a living person with a body trained to endure poison. Only a taster qualifies. Emotional beat: destiny arriving disguised as a death sentence.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara refuses and starts back down the mountain, deciding the kingdom chose its god when it prayed. But at the tree line she finds villages emptied—not taken, but walked willingly into the hills, smiling, to feed their god. Emotional beat: the moral floor dropping away.

chapters.title: The Eleventh Turn
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV. The presence, now nearly whole, parades the king before crowds whose worship feeds it openly. Aldric, buried deep, feels Mara's name surface like a bubble in black water. Emotional beat: a hostage remembering there is a world.

chapters.title: Sera's Choice
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Sera catches up to Mara at last—but has seen the emptied villages herself, and her own reports were used to steer worshippers to the god. She defects, bringing the court's secret archives. Emotional beat: an enemy becoming an ally through shared shame.

chapters.title: What the Archives Say
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. In the archives: the first binding was performed by a taster—the founder of Mara's own office—who swallowed the god's hunger and bought the kingdom thirty years. Every taster since has unknowingly kept the seal strong by consuming what the god touched. Emotional beat: Mara's whole life recontextualized.

chapters.title: The Founder's Recipe
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Following the founder's notes, Mara learns the unbinding isn't suicide: the hunger can be held, starved, and passed into salt if the vessel survives thirteen days without praying, hoping, or belonging to anything. Emotional beat: terror braided with a thread of possibility.

chapters.title: Invisible by Design
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Preparation chapter: Mara severs every tie—burns her map, resigns her post, refuses farewell—to become a person nothing can grip. Sera and Ivenna argue she needs anchors to survive. Emotional beat: loneliness chosen as armor.

chapters.title: The Twelfth Turn
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV. The god, sensing the plot, stops pretending: the king's body speaks with a voice like a landslide, and the court kneels weeping with love they cannot refuse. Isolde, horrified past complicity, sends a secret message to Mara. Emotional beat: the mask finally off.

chapters.title: Storming the Feast
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs interwoven. On the eve of the twelfth turn's feast, Mara returns not as a taster but as a guest, seated by Isolde's arrangement. Sera neutralizes the guard; Ivenna holds the shrine door. Emotional beat: all threads converging, hearts hammering.

chapters.title: The Toast
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The god offers Mara a goblet—her old role, her old comfort—and the court watches. Mara drinks, proving her immunity, then names the thing wearing the crown aloud before a thousand witnesses. Emotional beat: courage as simply refusing to look away.

chapters.title: Unbinding
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. With Ivenna's rites and the court as unwilling witnesses, Mara takes the god's hunger into herself. The extraction is described as being force-fed a decade of famines. The crown clatters empty; Aldric collapses, breathing. Emotional beat: agony transfigured into purpose.

chapters.title: Thirteen Days of Nothing
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Imprisoned gently in the shrine cell, Mara must starve the hunger without prayer, hope, or attachment. The god tempts her with visions of belonging—her mother's kitchen, the cook's laughter, a home. Emotional beat: endurance as the quietest heroism.

chapters.title: The Hunger Speaks
chapters.summary: The god's POV, rare and intimate. It argues with Mara from inside her ribs: it only ever answered prayers; it never lied; humans built it with their need. Emotional beat: the villain almost winning by being reasonable.

chapters.title: Day Nine: The Offer
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The hunger offers a bargain: release, and it will restore everyone the covenant consumed—including the cook, including the boy in the ravine. Mara nearly says yes. Emotional beat: the temptation of undoing grief.

chapters.title: Day Eleven: Visitors
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Against Ivenna's orders, Sera visits the cell, and her loyalty nearly undoes the fast—attachment feeds the hunger. Mara turns her away with words that wound them both. Emotional beat: love as a liability, refused on purpose.

chapters.title: Day Thirteen: Salt
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. At the final hour, starving and hollow, Mara pours the weakened hunger into the consecrated salt of the first shrine, sealing it as the founder once did—but this time with a lid that can be opened deliberately, not forever. Emotional beat: exhaustion, then unbearable lightness.

chapters.title: The King Who Remembers
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV. Freed, Aldric faces the wreckage of his reign and the families of the consumed. He does not abdicate; he kneels publicly and begins restitution, starting with the mountain shrines. Emotional beat: shame transformed into work.

chapters.title: Reckonings
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. The court reckons with its complicity: Isolde accepts exile to the shrines she helped starve; Sera burns the files used to herd worshippers and rebuilds the spycraft around protection rather than control. Emotional beat: institutions learning to blush.

chapters.title: The Taster's Office, Refounded
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Aldric asks Mara to lead a new order of tasters—not immune servants, but trained witnesses who taste, question, and testify. Mara rewrites the founder's recipe into something honest. Emotional beat: turning a cage into a craft.

chapters.title: What Belonging Costs
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara visits the ravine where the boy died and builds a cairn, then the cook's grave, leaving salt instead of flowers. She allows herself, at last, to grieve what survival cost. Emotional beat: mourning as the final act of courage.

chapters.title: Prayers, Answered Carefully
chapters.summary: Ivenna's POV. The old gods answer again—but now through the sealed salt, rationed and witnessed, giving just enough to remind the kingdom that faith is a meal shared, not a feast devoured. Emotional beat: cautious grace.

chapters.title: The Fourteenth Moon
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. One month after the unbinding, Mara walks the Thornfell roads openly for the first time, greeted by name at every shrine. The moon rises full and ordinary. Emotional beat: visibility embraced, fear set down.

chapters.title: Cyrus and the Salt
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, closing frame. Teaching her first apprentice—a sharp-tongued border girl—Mara tells the story of Cyrus, the forgotten founder-taster, and the salt that holds a god. The apprentice asks if the seal will hold. Mara answers: 'As long as someone keeps tasting honestly.' Emotional beat: legacy, continuity, and earned peace.
